newsitem.title: FRANCE: New EU Parliament leader elected despite protest.
newsitem.headline: New EU Parliament leader elected despite protest.

text.p: Spanish conservative Jose Maria Gil-Robles Gil Delgado was elected president of the European Parliament on Tuesday and was told immediately to change the methods which got him there.

A surprisingly large protest vote of almost one third of the assembly for his only challenger, France's Catherine Lalumiere, confirmed the deep dissatisfaction with the way the presidency has become the prerogative of the parliament's two biggest groups.
Gil-Robles, a member of the Partido Popular, gained 338 votes to Lalumiere's 177.

"Almost a third of the members of this parliament have voted in protest at this election -- you should be aware of that," Liberal leader Gijs De Vries told Gil-Robles after the results were announced.
His first words after taking the chair included thanks to Lalumiere, a former Council of Europe Secretary General.
"I think the votes she gained have only increased her prestige in this house," he said of the leader of the parliament's alternative European Radical Alliance group.
Under a long-standing deal the Socialists and mainly Christian Democrat European People's Party share the presidency of the parliament's five year legislature between them.
Jean-Claude Pasty, the leader of the assembly's third biggest group -- the Union for Europe -- told Gil-Robles he should take steps to wipe out this monopoly.
The election had worsened the lack of democracy the parliament regularly complained about in the other EU institutions, he said.
Gil-Robles said he would carry on fighting for democracy.
